title: 🤝 The Recruitment Drive — NDRC 1
foot: 🤝 NDRC 1 · The Recruitment Drive — B1–B2 · self-marking 🤝
story: Emma is a second-year sales student (BTS NDRC). This month, her class runs a “recruitment drive”: the students visit local companies to present their program and find apprenticeship partners. Every morning, Emma prepares her pitch, checks her appointments and calls the companies on her list.

Last Tuesday, Emma visited a logistics company near Dijon. She met the HR manager, presented the program and gave him a short brochure. The manager liked the idea, but he asked about the cost and the working hours. Emma stayed calm and proposed a flexible schedule.

Since the start of the drive, Emma has contacted fifteen companies and has signed three partnerships. She hasn't reached her target yet, but she has already learned a lot about negotiation. “A good salesperson listens more than they talk,” her tutor has told her many times. 🤝

sections.instr: Lis la phrase française et choisis la bonne traduction. Le repère de temps t'indique le temps à utiliser.

sections.name: RS Reported
sections.heading: Reported speech — what did they say?
sections.instr: Passe du discours direct au discours rapporté (backshift des temps, modaux, pronoms).

items.text: “I will call you tomorrow,” Emma said. → Emma said she ___ me the next day.
“I have finished the brochure,” he said. → He said he ___ the brochure.
“We are hiring two apprentices,” the manager said. → The manager said they ___ two apprentices.
“I can start in September,” she said. → She said she ___ start in September.
“Do you have a tutor?” he asked. → He asked if I ___ a tutor.
“Send me the file,” she said. → She told me ___ the file.
“I visited the company yesterday,” Emma said. → Emma said she ___ the company the day before.
“We don't work on Sundays,” they said. → They said they ___ on Sundays.

sections.name: NG Negotiation
sections.heading: Choose the right expression
sections.instr: Lis le but entre parenthèses, puis choisis l'expression la plus adaptée. Les trois sont du bon anglais, mais une seule convient à la situation.

items.text: (You want to open the meeting politely.)
options: Thank you for seeing me today. Shall we start?
You finally found time for me.
items.answer: Thank you for seeing me today. Shall we start?

items.text: (The manager says the program is expensive. You want to stay flexible.)
options: I understand. Could we look at the options together?
items.answer: I understand. Could we look at the options together?

items.text: (The manager asks for a discount you cannot give. Refuse politely.)
options: I'm afraid I can't go that low, but I can offer flexible hours.
items.answer: I'm afraid I can't go that low, but I can offer flexible hours.

items.text: (You want to propose a compromise.)
options: How about we meet halfway on the schedule?
items.answer: How about we meet halfway on the schedule?

items.text: (The manager hesitates. You want to reassure him.)
options: Don't worry — our team will support the apprentice every week.
If you don't decide now, you'll regret it.
Honestly, I'm not sure it will work.
items.answer: Don't worry — our team will support the apprentice every week.

items.text: (You need more time to think about an offer.)
options: Could I get back to you by Friday?
I'll decide right now, no matter what.
items.answer: Could I get back to you by Friday?

items.text: (You want to understand what matters most to the manager.)
options: What is the most important point for you?
Just sign here, the details don't matter.
Why are you making this so difficult?
items.answer: What is the most important point for you?

items.text: (You want to close the deal on good terms.)
options: Great — shall we put this in writing?
You'd better not change your mind.
items.answer: Great — shall we put this in writing?
